42. // CacheView - Abstract Specification Model
43. //==================================================================================================
44. 
45. /// Abstract view of a bounded LRU cache.
46. ///
47. /// - `contents`: the key-value mapping of all cached entries.
48. /// - `capacity`: maximum number of entries.
49. /// - `lru_order`: keys ordered from LRU (index 0) to MRU (last element).
50. #[verifier::ext_equal]
51. #[verifier::reject_recursive_types(K)]
52. #[verifier::reject_recursive_types(V)]
53. pub struct CacheView<K, V> {
54.     pub contents: Map<K, V>,
55.     pub capacity: nat,
56.     pub lru_order: Seq<K>,
57. }
58. 
59. impl<K, V> CacheView<K, V> {
60. 
61.     //----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
62.     // Well-formedness Invariant
63.     //----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
64. 
65.     /// Well-formedness invariant for the abstract cache state.
66.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
67.         // Size never exceeds capacity.
68.         &&& self.contents.dom().len() <= self.capacity
69.         // LRU order has no duplicates.
70.         &&& self.lru_order.no_duplicates()
71.         // LRU order contains exactly the stored keys.
72.         &&& self.lru_order.to_set() == self.contents.dom()
73.         // Explicit cardinality link (helps the solver).
74.         &&& self.lru_order.len() == self.contents.dom().len()
75.     }
76. 
77.     //----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
78.     // Helper Spec Functions
79.     //----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
80. 
81.     /// Move `key` to the most-recently-used position (end of the sequence).
82.     /// Preserves all other elements and their relative order.
83.     pub open spec fn move_to_mru(self, key: K) -> Seq<K> {
84.         self.lru_order.filter(|k: K| k != key).push(key)
85.     }
86. 
87.     //----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
88.     // Spec Transition Functions
89.     //----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
90. 
91.     /// Spec transition for `Cache::new`.
92.     pub open spec fn spec_new(capacity: nat) -> CacheView<K, V> {
93.         CacheView {
94.             contents: Map::empty(),
95.             capacity,
96.             lru_order: Seq::empty(),
97.         }
98.     }
99. 
100.     /// Spec transition for `Cache::get`.
101.     /// Returns the updated cache state and the lookup result.
102.     pub open spec fn spec_get(self, key: K) -> (CacheView<K, V>, Option<V>) {
103.         if self.contents.dom().contains(key) {
104.             (CacheView {
105.                 lru_order: self.move_to_mru(key),
106.                 ..self
107.             }, Some(self.contents[key]))
108.         } else {
109.             (self, None)
110.         }
111.     }
112. 
113.     /// Spec transition for `Cache::put`.
114.     pub open spec fn spec_put(self, key: K, value: V) -> CacheView<K, V> {
115.         if self.capacity == 0 {
116.             // Zero-capacity cache: no-op.
117.             self
118.         } else if self.contents.dom().contains(key) {
119.             // Overwrite existing key: replace value, refresh recency.
120.             CacheView {
121.                 contents: self.contents.insert(key, value),
122.                 lru_order: self.move_to_mru(key),
123.                 ..self
124.             }
125.         } else if self.contents.dom().len() >= self.capacity {
126.             // At capacity with new key: evict LRU victim, then insert.
127.             let victim = self.lru_order[0];
128.             CacheView {
129.                 contents: self.contents.remove(victim).insert(key, value),
130.                 lru_order: self.lru_order.subrange(1, self.lru_order.len() as int).push(key),
131.                 ..self
132.             }
133.         } else {
134.             // Below capacity with new key: insert directly.
135.             CacheView {
136.                 contents: self.contents.insert(key, value),
137.                 lru_order: self.lru_order.push(key),
138.                 ..self
139.             }
140.         }
141.     }
142. 
143.     /// Spec transition for `Cache::remove`.
144.     pub open spec fn spec_remove(self, key: K) -> CacheView<K, V> {
145.         if self.contents.dom().contains(key) {
146.             CacheView {
147.                 contents: self.contents.remove(key),
148.                 lru_order: self.lru_order.filter(|k: K| k != key),
149.                 ..self
150.             }
151.         } else {
152.             // Key absent: no-op.
153.             self
154.         }
155.     }
156. 
157.     /// Spec transition for `Cache::clear`.
158.     pub open spec fn spec_clear(self) -> CacheView<K, V> {
159.         CacheView {
160.             contents: Map::empty(),
161.             lru_order: Seq::empty(),
162.             ..self  // capacity preserved
163.         }
164.     }
165. }

# Verus Constraints

Study `docs/examples/binary-search/proof/` for a complete example following all
constraints below.

## Attribute Style for Exec Functions

All specs on **exec functions** must use the attribute-based syntax
(`#[verus_spec]`, `#[verus_verify]`, `proof! { }`, `proof_decl! { }`).
See the **verus-syntax** skill for the full reference and examples.

```rust
// ✅ CORRECT — attribute style for exec functions
#[verus_spec(ret =>
    requires x < 100,
    ensures ret == x + 1,
)]
fn foo(x: u32) -> u32 {
    x + 1
}

// ❌ WRONG — do not wrap exec functions in verus! { }
verus! {
    fn foo(x: u32) -> (ret: u32)
        requires x < 100,
        ensures ret == x + 1,
    { x + 1 }
} // verus!
```

**`verus! { }` blocks** are still used for:
- `spec fn` and `proof fn` definitions (in `.spec.rs` and `.proof.rs`)
- Type-level specs (`broadcast`, `impl View`, etc.)

Key benefit: exec function signatures stay unmodified — the original `fn`
signature is untouched, specs live in the attribute.

## Source Integrity (exec code)

The following rules apply to the original source files (e.g. `lib.rs`), not to
`*.spec.rs` / `*.proof.rs` which are freely editable.

Verus verification is **in-place**: specs and proofs are added directly alongside
exec code. The annotated code remains fully compilable and runnable — Verus
constructs are erased during normal `cargo build` via cfg-gating. Keep changes
minimal so developers can review diffs easily.

**Preserve by default:** exec logic, function signatures, struct definitions,
comments, debug assertions, and all other existing code.

**Minimal equivalent rewrites** are allowed when Verus genuinely cannot express
a construct. The escalation ladder (each step requires exhausting the previous):

1. **Verify as-is** — most code works with Verus directly.
2. **Search vstd** — your training data is likely outdated. `grep -r` the entire
   vstd directory. Check `std_specs/`, recent additions.
3. **Minimal equivalent rewrite** — rewrite the smallest possible expression
   to an equivalent one Verus accepts. Requirements:
   - Same semantics (identical observable behavior for all inputs)
   - Same panic/error behavior
   - Same asymptotic time and space complexity
   - Smallest possible diff
   - `// VERUS REWRITE: <reason>` comment on the changed code
   - Minimal reproducer proving the original is unsupported
4. **Stdlib wrapper** — if a stdlib/core function call fails because Verus
   cannot handle the parameter types (e.g., `&mut [T]` from `DerefMut`
   coercion, closures), create a thin wrapper function whose body contains
   **ONLY** the stdlib call. Mark the wrapper `external_body` with pre/post
   conditions. The original function calls the wrapper instead. This isolates
   the trust boundary to the thinnest possible layer.

   Example — `core::mem::replace` on `&mut Vec<T>[index]`:
   ```rust
   #[verus_verify(external_body)]
   #[verus_spec(prev =>
       requires index < old(v)@.len(),
       ensures
           prev == old(v)@[index as int],
           v@ == old(v)@.update(index as int, value),
           v@.len() == old(v)@.len(),
   )]
   fn vec_replace<T>(v: &mut Vec<T>, index: usize, value: T) -> T {
       ::core::mem::replace(&mut v[index], value)
   }
   ```
   The wrapper body is a single stdlib call. The `external_body` trusts only
   this one line. The calling function remains fully body-verified.

5. **`external_body` on the original** — absolute last resort. Requires a
   minimal reproducer and `trust.md` entry.

**Principle:** prefer rewriting code to a semantic equivalent over ANY cheating.
A rewrite that lets Verus verify the body is always better than `external_body`.

**Never cfg-gate away and duplicate exec definitions.** Adding
`#[cfg(not(verus_keep_ghost))]` to a function, impl block, struct, enum, or
constant and providing a verus-annotated copy is forbidden — it verifies the
